title: COMPSCI 61B or COMPSCI 61BL (Data Structures)
description: A second programming course on data structures, such as lists, trees, hash tables, and graphs, and the algorithms that use them, with attention to efficiency and program design.
notes: Choice slot: Berkeley's COMPSCI 61B or its lab-based version 61BL. Official descriptions are in data/raw/ucb/courses/.

title: COMPSCI 61C or COMPSCI 61CL (Great Ideas of Computer Architecture)
description: A course on how computers work below the programming language: data representation, machine instructions, memory, caches, and parallelism.
notes: Choice slot: Berkeley's COMPSCI 61C or its lab-based version 61CL (61CL is not in the 2026-27 catalog). Official description of 61C is in data/raw/ucb/courses/.

title: PHYSICS 7A or PHYSICS 5A (Physics for Scientists and Engineers)
description: A calculus-based introductory physics course on mechanics: motion, forces, energy, momentum, and rotation.
notes: Choice slot: Berkeley's PHYSICS 7A or 5A. Official descriptions are in data/raw/ucb/courses/.

title: PHYSICS 7B or PHYSICS 5B + PHYSICS 5BL (Physics for Scientists and Engineers)
description: A calculus-based introductory physics course on electricity and magnetism, sometimes with heat, waves, or optics, and in some versions a separate laboratory.
notes: Choice slot: Berkeley's PHYSICS 7B, or PHYSICS 5B with lab 5BL. Official descriptions are in data/raw/ucb/courses/.

title: ELENG 66 or ELENG 64 (Introduction to Signals, Dynamics, and Information)
description: An introductory electrical engineering course for majors in electrical engineering and computer science, on topics such as signals and systems, circuits, and devices.
notes: Berkeley requires both ELENG 66 and ELENG 64, in either order; each listing is one of the pair. Official descriptions are in data/raw/ucb/courses/.

title: Reading & Composition Part A
description: A first-year writing course on reading closely and writing clear, well-argued essays.
notes: Berkeley: approved R&C course, part of the Humanities/Social Sciences requirement.

title: Reading & Composition Part B
description: A second writing course on research-based argument, building on the first.
notes: Berkeley: approved R&C course, part of the Humanities/Social Sciences requirement.

title: Humanities/Social Sciences course
description: A general education course in the humanities or social sciences, such as history, philosophy, literature, economics, or psychology.
notes: Berkeley: four approved H/SS courses beyond the two R&C courses.

title: Natural Science Elective
description: A natural science course chosen from an approved list, such as biology, chemistry, astronomy, or further physics.
notes: Berkeley: one course from the list in note 1.

title: Ethics/Social Implications of Technology
description: A course on ethics in engineering and computing or on the social effects of technology.
notes: Berkeley: one course from the list in note 6.

title: EECS Upper Division Technical Electives
description: Upper-level courses in electrical engineering and computer science chosen by the student, such as operating systems, compilers, databases, machine learning, or circuits, including at least one design course.
notes: Berkeley: at least 20 upper-division EECS units (20 in the plan).

title: Free Electives
description: Any course the student chooses that counts toward the degree, inside or outside the major.
notes: Berkeley: 12 units in the plan; more may be needed to reach the 120-unit minimum.
